title: Collective Quantum State Preparation Is Nonadditive
authors: Lin Zhu, Ranyiliu Chen, Xin Wang, Shenggen Zheng
abstract: Quantum state preparation is a basic primitive of quantum computation and control, but its resource cost is usually analyzed for one target state or under an independent-copy construction. Here we study the many-copy problem under weighted Pauli control, where a Pauli-product rotation $e^{iφP}$ is charged by its rotation angle $|φ|$, independently of the weight of $P$. We derive the exact single-qubit preparation cost and show that it is strictly nonadditive: a four-pulse collective protocol prepares two $T$ states at lower cost than two optimal one-copy protocols. We further identify finite regions of the Bloch sphere with collective saving, including trajectories that remain product throughout, showing that transient entanglement is not the only mechanism behind the advantage. Complementarily, a dimension-independent Rényi-entropy speed limit gives an extensive lower bound for every coherent target and an exponential fidelity penalty below a finite preparation rate. These results establish a many-copy geometry of state synthesis in which uncorrelated outputs can nevertheless benefit from collective control.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the resource cost of preparing multiple copies of a quantum state using collective quantum control. It proves that this cost is strictly nonadditive, meaning that coordinating the preparation of several copies can achieve the target state at a lower total cost than preparing each copy individually. This establishes a new 'many-copy geometry' for state synthesis in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the resource cost for preparing multiple copies of a quantum state (the many-copy problem) is additive when using collective quantum control.
main_result: Collective state preparation is shown to be strictly nonadditive, meaning the asymptotic cost per copy can be lower than the cost of preparing a single copy.
method: The authors derive exact single-qubit preparation cost formulas and use entropy bounds (Rényi entropy) to establish lower bounds on the preparation rate.
model_or_system: The model uses quantum state preparation governed by Pauli-product rotations $e^{i\phi P}$, where the cost is the total rotation angle $\sum |\phi_j|$. The analysis focuses on comparing single-copy costs ($C_1$) versus collective/asymptotic costs ($C_\infty$).
key_observables: Minimum preparation cost ($C_n(\psi)$), asymptotic cost per copy ($C_\infty(\psi)$), and fidelity bounds ($F_n$).
important_parameters: The Bloch vector coordinates $(x, y, z)$, the number of copies $n$, and the Pauli weight $P$.
main_assumptions: The cost metric assumes the rotation angle $|\phi|$ is charged independently of the Pauli weight $P$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the cost comparison for preparing two T states using both independent and collective protocols, and show the evolution of concurrence along the circuit.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the nonadditivity of the cost for simple cases (like the T state), then derives general cost formulas, and finally uses entropy bounds to constrain the achievable collective savings.
why_interesting: The finding that collective control can yield non-additive advantages in state synthesis provides a new geometric understanding of resource costs beyond simple independent operations, which is crucial for designing efficient quantum protocols.
